sourceInformation.source: Mad Men (2007-2015), the AMC television drama created by Matthew Weiner
sourceInformation.genre: Narrative adventure / office life sim with a card-and-timing pitch battle
sourceInformation.perspective: Three-quarter top-down (engine threequarter view), switchable to isometric and top-down in the office
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.1 (full engine from the handoff package), plain JavaScript, AI Hub session client 1.3.0 (protocol 1); bundled into one HTML file with a small Node script
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine-native retro-modern pixel art: PS1-era resolution, shaded HD Humanoid rigs, furniture as data shapes, canvas lighting, in a mid-century palette of walnut, teal, mustard and orange
sourceInformation.animation: Engine-native procedural Humanoid rigs (walk cycles, idle breathing, poses, expressions, live dialog portraits) plus engine scripts and tweens
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written jazz loops on the engine chip synth (title, office bossa, pitch, closer, evening ballad, win and lose stings), synthesized sound effects, and Simlish gibberish voices pitched per character
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 in ghost mode (1-4 players: seeded deal, shared positions shown as ghosts, progress and results); local 2-4 player hot-seat Pitch-Off offline
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium via Playwright (scripted play-throughs, faked DualSense gamepad), WebKit iPhone emulation for the touch-only gate, AI Hub harness automatic runs (2 players; 4 players with latency, jitter and loss; host-leave), viewport-matrix across 24 device/engine combinations; no real phone, real controller or real iOS Safari
sourceInformation.research: None online beyond the engine and AI Hub documentation; the source drawn from general knowledge
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: 13 issues: a mouse hint overflowed its box; AIHub.ready() never sent because a game.after() timer was cleared by the scene change; the touch-only gate never showed; leaving the attract demo during a pitch left the game stuck on the pitch screen; keys outside the bindings did not end the attract demo; Enter both chose a card and skipped the creative meeting; the pitch could be won with one card; the projector screen was out of frame; prompts overlapped; the objection box overflowed; a name label stayed over dialog; a bad material name; floors too busy.

3 critical: the AI Hub round never starting (ready never sent), touch-only devices getting a menu they could not use, and the attract demo leaving the game stuck on the pitch screen when exited mid-pitch.

The AI Hub harness in automatic mode, and a 28-item per-feature checklist script run against the final bundle (campaign, Pitch-Off with 2, 3 and 4 players, controller settings, attract mode, touch-only gate).
The viewport-matrix run of the title screen across 24 devices: all clean, it found nothing.
engineFeedback: Shapes as data (a whole 1964 office from a few lines per desk), the Dialog box with live portraits and choices, and coroutine scripts on game time, which made the pitch sequence easy to write.

Yes: game.after() timers are cleared by game.go(), so a ready() scheduled that way never fired; and input.lastDevice defaults to keyboard, so it cannot be used to detect a touch-only device. Also Enter is bound to both start and confirm, which caused a double action.
The pitch system: the card battle against objections, the delivery timing meter, the hold-and-release closer with projector slides, plus the attract-mode bot and the AI Hub ghost layer.
Controller prompts: input.label() returns PlayStation symbols the pixel font cannot draw, so every button glyph had to be hand drawn.
The overlapping default bindings of the menu actions (Enter as both start and confirm, Escape as both pause and cancel).
A built-in prompt widget that draws the right glyph (PlayStation shapes, Xbox letters, key caps, mouse) for the last device used.
promptFeedback: The freedom to choose the genre, which let Mad Men become a game about talking, drinking and pitching rather than a forced action game.
The multiplayer line: AI Hub integration plus multiplayer for the game on its own was ambiguous; I read the second as local hot seat.
Fitting attract mode, local versus, AI Hub sessions and a three-day story with endings into one polished vertical slice.
A real DualSense on a real TV at ten feet, to judge text size, glyphs and pacing as the prompt intends.

aiHub.name: Mad Mention
aiHub.tagline: Win the room. Hold the pause.
aiHub.description: Walk a 1964 Madison Avenue agency gathering ideas before two o'clock, then pitch them to the client: answer each objection with the right appeal and deliver your tagline on the beat.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD walk, Cross/E talk, Triangle/Tab ideas, Square/V view; in the pitch pick an idea and press on the gold
